title: Rumors of Covert Activity
text: “I wonder if that’s also damage from the Waves? I’m not sure if the Waves are actually the cause, though.”
“Waves are occurring in other countries too, aren’t they? It’s conceivable that this happened separately from the Dragon Hourglass we’re registered to, but…”
“Yeah, honestly… when you think it’s because of the Waves, it does kind of fit that theory. Ren, Itsuki, Motoyasu-kun—do you two know anything?”
“Can’t say I don’t…”
“There were some flavor-text type descriptions that gave off that sort of ominous vibe, but…”
Hmm, indeed. Now that I think of it, I believe I heard something in Cal Mira Island’s tourist information about old ghost stories tied to the island’s past Waves.
“Starting with this incident… well, one after another, people started disappearing throughout Melromarc, including soldiers. Apparently that’s what led to the reinforced conscription.”
“In a sense, even the honorable human citizens themselves are being conscripted, then?”
“That’s true, but… some of the slaves have been affected too. Honestly, a fair amount of it might be getting pinned on us.”
“Oh? And in what sense would that be?”
Itsuki asked as though he had no idea what she could mean.
“Well, first there were those Three Heroes Church guys disguised as bandits—we captured them alive and sold them off, didn’t we?”
“Indeed we did.”
They served nicely as a funding source until the circus got on its feet. We sold them off to Siltvelt one after another, I say.
“That died down after a while, sure. But then… next there was an incident where nobles started disappearing in the same way.”
At that point in Father’s explanation, Itsuki turned his face away. That would be because you were the one making them disappear and hauling them back as ‘souvenirs’ to sell in Siltvelt, wouldn’t it?
“And apparently there was also an incident at a fort, which may or may not be Wave-related…”
“With personnel numbers dropping that much… this is our chance, Naofumi-san. Let’s rally the troops and crush Siltvelt.”

“No, no, no, Itsuki… we’re doing all sorts of things in Siltvelt specifically to prevent that from happening, letting off steam and whatnot. Wolf’s even out there giving speeches in Siltvelt, telling everyone to stay calm.”
Talk about putting the cart before the horse. Itsuki clicked his tongue.
“And yet it’s such a perfect chance…”
“Don’t forget why we were summoned in the first place. Our goal isn’t to wage war and conquer the world.”
“Well… I suppose you’re right.”
Itsuki seemed to be joking, but his remarks were suspiciously aggressive lately.

“For what it’s worth, when I disguise myself as Sword Hero and go around gathering information from guilds in various regions, plenty of people are whispering that the demi-humans and beastmen are working in the shadows to weaken our nation’s military strength. Even though they keep investigating Shield Hero’s place over and over, they can’t seem to find any tail to grab.”
Father looked away too. There was no denying that our forces were indeed being weakened. And right now, the main cause of that was Itsuki running around doing all sorts of things.
“People can cook up any accusation they like, honestly… but even so, we don’t have nearly enough strength to march on Siltvelt. In a sense, isn’t pushing this into all-out war rather difficult?”
To begin with, this was a period where the Queen was barely managing to smooth things over through diplomacy.
“Regardless of demi-human or beastman, there’s a chance nearby countries might just invade outright. Depending on how things go, we might have no choice but to act ourselves, so let’s stay prepared.”
“Problems just keep piling up…”
“Itsuki, during the next Wave or whatever, even if there are conscripted demi-humans and beastmen there, let’s make sure we end things quickly so no one gets hurt.”
“Right. Forcing people to fight against their will never leads anywhere good.”

And so, having secured Fleon-chan’s egg, we shared the current state of affairs in Melromarc among ourselves. By the way, it seemed Father had already arranged the Wave equipment with the old man at the weapon shop, indeed.

And so, with the heroes’ unity already solidified more than any preparations for the Wave, the circus continued making its way through Melromarc as though there were nothing left to fear. It was right around then. With Father remaining a virgin for far too long, I had to stay vigilant day and night against the danger of Rival showing up out of nowhere, worming her way in, and pouncing on him. So I went and asked Older Sister, who happened to be in the tent while Panda was off in Zeltoble. Incidentally, Itsuki had gone off happily hand-in-hand with Mole for a stroll through the town of Zeltoble—said they were off to get a meal. Watching the two of them looking so cozy together, I couldn’t shake the feeling that Father simply lacked whatever atmosphere was needed for “something” to happen afterward.
“Older Sister! How is progress coming along with Father, if I may ask?”

I posed the question to Older Sister, who had recently taken charge of looking after Big Sister and the others over in Zeltoble. Father would come visit Zeltoble regularly, sometimes staying overnight at our base there, and had even gone out drinking with Older Sister, Panda, and Elephant. Incidentally, while Older Sister performed in the Zeltoble circus, she’d also apparently started appearing in the Coliseum as a sort of publicity stunt, whipping the crowds of Zeltoble into a frenzy. Since Panda and Elephant were often away on business in Melromarc, that seemed to be funneling extra popularity her way. On top of that, Father’s subordinates Crocodile Guy and Wolf had also started appearing from time to time and were gradually becoming something of a talking point. Apparently there had recently been a match between Crocodile Guy and Older Sister that turned into quite the legendary bout.
“Oh my? Motoyasu-chan. Asking about Naofumi-chan and me? We’ve just been having fun drinking together—Sasa-chan wanted to cut loose, so we all went out together, and it was a blast.”
“That’s not what I meant. I mean with Father specifically, indeed.”
“Oh my~? Naofumi-chan can really hold his liquor, you know. Sister has so much fun with him.”
Older Sister’s response was as unchanged as ever. Somehow I simply couldn’t picture any relationship having actually developed there. So I decided to ask directly.
“Then has Older Sister spent any enjoyable time with Father as, shall we say, a man and a woman? I would of course be happy to set the stage.”
“Oh my~… Sister’s had plenty of fun times with Naofumi-chan, we’ve done heaps of drinking contests together. Naofumi-chan really can hold his liquor, isn’t that wonderful?”

…This was undoubtedly still white. Far, far too wholesome. Older Sister was supposed to be the predatory type through and through, and yet it seemed that getting involved with Father required not just certain conditions, but practically someone taking that first decisive step. At minimum, it seemed one party had to be sufficiently weakened before things could progress at all. And the trouble was, Father could hardly be called the predatory type either. Someone like a reincarnator such as Takt would start behaving just like a pig the moment some pig so much as whispered sweet nothings at him, but Father was, after all, human. Hmm… it occurred to me to wonder how the Filolial-samas might handle this, but I decided not to think about it. As embodiments of love itself, once they take a liking to someone they go full throttle—dances of love, cheerful songs, gentle affection, that’s simply how Filolial-sama operate, indeed.
“Panda! And what about you, might I ask!?”

Lately I’d noticed Father getting along quite nicely with Panda. He’d use her lazy, sprawled-out form as a backrest while doing paperwork, and even give her massages and groom her fur at night. If Panda simply transformed into her wolf form and pounced right then and there, there was no doubt Father would finally get some experience under his belt.
“What the heck are you even asking? What exactly are you expecting outta me here?”
“Simply what we agreed upon in our very first negotiation! You’re to heal Father. It’s not enough to only receive healing—you must give something back in return, indeed.”

“Beats me. All he does is take care of me whenever I’m being lazy, that’s it. If anything, it’s him who’s the problem—getting me plastered, escorting me all the way home, and then doing absolutely nothing after that!”

So, in other words, Panda would reciprocate if asked, but the issue was that Father simply left afterward without doing anything, leaving her frustrated? Gah… Father, being the herbivore type simply will not do, I say! Does this mean he’s so dense that he fails to pick up on his partner’s subtle cues, thereby failing to respond even when the other party throws him a direct pitch!? How utterly oblivious. Hm? For a moment I thought I heard countless voices somewhere shouting “Look who’s talking!” along with the squealing of pigs, but surely that was just my imagination. I do, after all, carry the sins of my own past relationships with various parties! Gah… whatever shall I do? At this rate, Rival will eventually return and simply gobble Father right up. I’m fast approaching the limit of how leisurely I can afford to sit back and watch this unfold. In that case…
